problem:
A bungee jumping instructor measures how much a bungee rope stretches (in meters) when one end of the rope is attached to the bridge railing while a weight of $x$ kilograms is hung on the other. This data is shown below.

| Weight $(x)$ | **$10$** | **$20$** | **$30$** | **$40$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stretch $(y)$ | $1$ | $1.5$ | $2$ | $2.5$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, how much will the rope stretch if the instructor uses a $65$-kilogram mass, assuming the trend continues?  

*Hint: You can use the fact that* 

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{500}[\begin{aligned}750 & -25 \\ -25 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 200\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*

feedback.problem:
A statistician collected data on the height above the ground (in hundreds of meters) of a hot air balloon during the first five minutes of its flight. This data is shown below. 

| Time $(x)$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Height $(y)$ | $1.6$ | $3.0$ | $4.6$ | $6$ | $7.6$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the balloon's height after $6$ minutes, assuming the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}22.8 \\ 83.4\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
feedback.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1.6 \\ 3.0 \\ 4.6 \\ 6 \\ 7.6\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}22.8 \\ 83.4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.06 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=0.06+1.5x.$

Finally, to predict the height of the balloon after $6$ minutes, we substitute $x=6$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =0.06+1.5(6) \\  & =9.06\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the balloon's height after $6$ minutes will be $906$ meters.  

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=6$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.
